---
title: "baltimore events"
format: html
editor: visual
---

## 

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(showtext)
font_add_google("Poppins", "poppins")
showtext_auto()

# Read data
events <- read_csv("events.csv")

# Long format
events_long <- events %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(`Baltimore Convention Center event`, `Orioles home game`, `Ravens home game`),
    names_to = "venue",
    values_to = "event"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Date = as.Date(Date),
    # create a categorical fill: venue name when there is an event, otherwise "None"
    fill = if_else(event == "yes", venue, "None")
  )

# define colors for categories (including a "None" color)
fill_colors <- c(
  "Baltimore Convention Center event" = "#1E90FF",
  "Orioles home game" = "#FF7F00",
  "Ravens home game" = "#800080",
  "None" = "white"
)

# build the plot and save into an object
ggplot(events_long, aes(x = Date, y = venue, fill = fill)) +
  # set width to 1 day so tiles look like daily blocks; set height so rows are readable
  geom_tile(width = 1, height = 0.8, color = "gray90") +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Event",
    values = fill_colors,
    breaks = c("Baltimore Convention Center event", "Orioles home game", "Ravens home game"),
    labels = c("Convention Center", "Orioles game", "Ravens game")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Event Days by Venue (2024)",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Venue"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "poppins") +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 10)
  )
```

```{r}
ggsave("heatmap.svg", plot = heatmap, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300, device = "svg")
```

```{r}
write_csv(events_long, "events_long.csv")
```

```{r}
events <- events |>
  mutate(
    all_vacant = if_all(
      c(`Baltimore Convention Center event`, `Orioles home game`, `Ravens home game`),
      ~ .x == "no"
    )
  )

events |>
  filter(all_vacant == "TRUE") |> 
  summarize(count = n())
```
